name: Hottentot Dutch
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: den Besten, Hans. 2009. In search of a submerged phonology: the case of early Cape Dutch Pidgin. In R. Selbach, H. C. Cardoso & M. van den Berg (eds.), Gradual creolization: studies celebrating Jacques Arends (Creole Language Library 34), 219-241. Amsterdam: Benjamins. DOI 10.1075/cll.34.16bes [UvA-DARE submitted manuscript, 21 pp.]
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent in the pidgin. The whole paper is segmental: evidence for a 'Khoekhoe Dutch accent' in CDP = [b/d/g]~[p/t/k] voicing allophony, word-internal [b]~[v], word-final [t]-deletion, [l]~[r] allophony, syllable-final [r]-deletion, a possible paragogic schwa (sections 2-5, concl. p.13 of ms). The only occurrence of 'stress' (fn. 22) concerns how an Icelandic observer (Olafsson 1623) may have reshaped a remembered Khoekhoe/pidgin word to initial stress in Icelandic fashion -- not a statement about CDP prosody. Author stresses the data are fragmentary written records up to…
